title: Validating and Testing Workflow Changes knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Validating and Testing Workflow Changes?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Validate workflow changes with YAML/schema checks, tests, controlled runs, failure-path checks, and review of permissions and event filters.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Validate workflow changes with YAML/schema checks, tests, controlled runs, failure-path checks, and review of permissions and event filters.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of validating and testing workflow changes: Validate workflow changes with YAML/schema checks, tests, controlled runs, failure-path checks, and review of permissions and event filters. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “YAML syntax validation”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
questions.answer_key: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level.
questions.explanation: YAML syntax validation: YAML is indentation-sensitive. Check that nested values are aligned, values have the expected type, special strings are quoted when needed, and the workflow schema accepts the key at that level. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to validating and testing workflow changes?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Validate workflow changes with YAML/schema checks, tests, controlled runs, failure-path checks, and review of permissions and event filters. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
